questions.question: If your rear wheel locks while braking on a good surface, you should:

options.text: Keep it locked until you stop completely.
Release the rear brake and use only the front brake.
Release the rear brake, then quickly apply it again.
Release the rear brake and shift to a lower gear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep it locked until you stop completely.
questions.explanation: If your rear brake locks on a good surface, keep it locked until you stop. Your motorcycle will still be controllable if it stays upright and travels straight.

questions.question: Your lane position should not:

options.text: Help you see and be seen better.
Provide you with an escape route.
Invite other drivers to share your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Invite other drivers to share your lane.
questions.explanation: Your lane position should keep you safe by helping you see and be seen, avoiding hazards, escaping from danger, and staying out of blind spots. Position yourself to discourage other drivers from entering your lane.

questions.question: When braking, you should use:

options.text: Both the front and rear brakes.
Either the front or rear brake, but not both.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both the front and rear brakes.
questions.explanation: Use both brakes every time you slow down or stop.

questions.question: When riding over rough surfaces, you should:

options.text: Hold the handgrips loosely to let them move freely.
Hold the handgrips firmly to stay in control.
Use a lot of throttle to get over the rough surface.
Ride without a helmet so it doesn't cover your face.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold the handgrips firmly to stay in control.
questions.explanation: Hold the handgrips firmly on rough surfaces. This keeps you in control of your motorcycle's direction.

questions.question: If a small animal enters your lane during traffic, you should:

options.text: Swerve into other lanes if needed to avoid the animal.
Switch lanes as quickly as possible.
Flash your lights to scare the animal away.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay in your lane.
questions.explanation: Avoid hitting an animal if you safely can. In traffic, stay in your lane. Swerving into another lane could cause you to hit another vehicle. Hitting a small animal is safer than hitting another vehicle.

questions.question: A properly-fitted motorcycle:

options.text: Lets you touch the ground with your feet while seated.
Has a seat level with your waist.
Has a seat 10 inches above your waist.
Has a seat 10 inches below your waist.

questions.correctAnswerText: Lets you touch the ground with your feet while seated.
questions.explanation: A proper fit lets you reach the ground with your feet while sitting on the seat. Keep your feet on the footrests when riding.

questions.question: Switching to a lower gear is also called:
questions.correctAnswerText: Engine braking.
questions.explanation: Shifting to a lower gear works like using the brakes. This is why downshifting is called engine braking.

questions.question: Brightly-colored helmets:

options.text: May help other drivers see you.

questions.correctAnswerText: May help other drivers see you.
questions.explanation: Choose a brightly-colored helmet. It protects you in a crash and helps other drivers see you better.

questions.question: The front brake provides about how much of a motorcycle's stopping power?
questions.correctAnswerText: About 70 percent
questions.explanation: The front brake is more powerful than the rear brake. It provides at least 70 percent of the motorcycle's total stopping power.

questions.question: Most crashes happen:
questions.correctAnswerText: On short trips.
questions.explanation: Most crashes happen on trips shorter than five miles, just a few minutes after the rider starts.

questions.question: If you cannot avoid a slippery surface, what should you do?

options.text: Speed up and lean the motorcycle.
Speed up and keep the motorcycle upright.
Slow down and lean the motorcycle.
Slow down and keep the motorcycle upright.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and keep the motorcycle upright.
questions.explanation: Keep your motorcycle upright and go as slowly as possible over a slippery surface.

questions.question: When choosing a helmet, which of these is NOT important?

options.text: It meets U.S. Department of Transportation standards.
It has no cracks or defects.

questions.correctAnswerText: It looks attractive.
questions.explanation: Choose a helmet that meets U.S. Department of Transportation and state standards, fits snugly, and has no cracks, loose padding, or frayed straps. How it looks is not important for safety.

questions.question: When you slow down or stop, you should use both brakes:

options.text: Only if the pavement is wet.
Only when riding in the city.

questions.correctAnswerText: Every time.
questions.explanation: Using both the front and rear brakes gives you the best stopping power. Use both brakes every time you slow down or stop.

questions.question: If your motorcycle starts to wobble, what should you do?

options.text: Grip the handlebars firmly and slowly release the throttle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Grip the handlebars firmly and slowly release the throttle.
questions.explanation: Do not speed up, as this makes the wobble worse. Instead, grip the handlebars firmly and slowly close the throttle. Move your weight forward and down, and pull off the road as soon as you can. Avoid braking, as it may also make the wobble worse.

questions.question: If you cannot avoid a slippery road, what should you do?

options.text: Lean into the slippery section to keep your balance.
Keep your speed to improve traction.
Do not worry about the road conditions.
Keep your motorcycle upright and go as slowly as needed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your motorcycle upright and go as slowly as needed.
questions.explanation: It is best to avoid slippery roads completely. If you cannot avoid one, keep your motorcycle upright and go as slowly as possible.

questions.question: For a face shield to work well, it should NOT:
questions.correctAnswerText: Be completely airtight.
questions.explanation: A good face shield should have no scratches, resist being broken, allow clear views to the sides, attach securely, and allow air to pass through. An airtight shield causes fogging and makes it hard to see.

questions.question: The front brake:

options.text: Provides less than half of your stopping power.
Provides about 70 percent of your stopping power.
Should only be used when it is wet.
Should be the only brake you use.

questions.correctAnswerText: Provides about 70 percent of your stopping power.
questions.explanation: The front brake is much more powerful than the rear brake. It provides at least 70 percent of your total stopping power. Use both brakes every time you slow down or stop.

questions.question: You will ______ hear a tire going flat.
questions.correctAnswerText: Seldom
questions.explanation: You will seldom hear your tire go flat. A sudden change in how your motorcycle handles is the more common sign of a tire problem.

questions.question: What type of footwear is best for riding a motorcycle?
questions.correctAnswerText: Sturdy boots
questions.explanation: Sturdy boots or shoes that cover your ankles provide the best protection. Laced-up boots or high-top heavy shoes work well. If your shoes have long laces, tuck them in securely before riding.

questions.question: Where is the front brake lever located?
questions.correctAnswerText: On the right handgrip
questions.explanation: The front brake lever is on the right handgrip. Learn where all your motorcycle's controls are before you start riding.
